newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL key share index at new 1997 low, still falling.
newsitem.headline: KL key share index at new 1997 low, still falling.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares continued falling in afternoon trading, easing more than 2.0 percent to a new 1997 low of 958.96 at 0702 GMT.
At 0707 GMT, the key Composite Index was down 2.12 percent or 20.72 points to 957.84.
Dealers said the heavy selling was triggered by Malaysia's huge trade deficit for June and curbs on swaps transactions on local banks.
"There is only bad news in a market already weak on sentiment," said a dealer with a bank-backed brokerage.
He said several local and foreign institutions were dumping local blue chip shares.
Malaysia announced a 2.8 billion ringgit deficit for June, the biggest in any one month in at least 17 years, analysts said.

On Sunday, Malaysia announced a limit of $2.0 million on local banks' currency swap exposure to any one overseas customer, a move seen by many analysts as regressive for the fast-growing and liberalising Malaysia.
Among index heavyweights losing heavily at 0713 GMT were Maybank, down 80 cents to 23.60 ringgit, Telekom, off 15 cents to 9.10 ringgit and Tenaga, down 25 cents to 9.85 ringgit.
Most other blue-chips were down between 10 and 50 cents.
